public_sources.title: Batch Invariance - vLLM
public_sources.relevance: Official current deterministic-serving contract: output can be made independent of batch size/order inside a supported domain, with explicit hardware/model limits and a performance tradeoff.

public_sources.title: Reproducibility - vLLM
public_sources.relevance: Official warning that default serving is not reproducible and even reproducible mode is scoped to the same hardware and vLLM version.

public_sources.title: Reproducibility - PyTorch 2.13
public_sources.relevance: Official warning that identical seeds do not guarantee reproducibility across releases/platforms and deterministic algorithms can be slower.

public_sources.title: LLM-42: Enabling Determinism in LLM Inference with Verified Speculation
public_sources.relevance: Primary evidence for deterministic-by-construction verify/rollback as an alternative to inferring equivalence from rare mismatches.

public_sources.title: CoRun: Padding is Simple and Efficient for Deterministic LLM Inference
public_sources.relevance: Recent primary evidence that deterministic inference can have large system-specific overhead, motivating direct measurement of the determinism tax.

public_sources.title: Estimating means of bounded random variables by betting
public_sources.relevance: Primary anytime-valid bounded-mean/betting foundation for mismatch monitoring under explicit stochastic assumptions.

public_sources.title: Anytime-Valid Inference Under Outcome Delay: A Design-Based Approach
public_sources.relevance: Primary evidence that timing and outcomes can be coupled, supporting explicit filtration/conditional assumptions rather than completed-sample intuition.

hierarchical_fallback_result.negative_result: An empirical parent-level mismatch upper bound is not, by itself, a valid conservative fallback for a sparse or unseen child stratum. A parent mixture can have a tiny marginal mismatch rate while one child has a much larger conditional mismatch rate and future evaluation concentrates on that child.
valid_parent_fallback_cases: A deterministic-by-construction runtime contract whose guarantee explicitly covers every child in the parent domain.
A predeclared structural worst-case bound epsilon_parent such that P(mismatch | child,past)<=epsilon_parent is guaranteed for all children covered by that parent.

A statistically justified hierarchical model that itself supplies a simultaneous/conditional upper guarantee for each child; ordinary pooled estimation or empirical-Bayes shrinkage alone is not such a guarantee.
hierarchical_fallback_result.fail_closed_rule: If no child-specific bound and no structurally valid parent bound exists, the child is uncertified for fastest stochastic hedging. Use canonical single-attempt inference or deterministic-by-construction execution instead of inheriting the pooled parent epsilon.
hierarchical_fallback_result.reason: The previous 95/5 A/B counterexample gives aggregate epsilon=.005 with a child epsilon=.10. If evaluation concentrates in that child, a p0=.505 paired-sign factor can have conditional expectation >1 and false crossing far above nominal.

degradation_monitor_design.target: Detect that a previously certified fingerprint/stratum's mismatch rate has risen above epsilon0=.005. This is an operational demotion alarm, distinct from evidence used to prove identity equivalence.
degradation_monitor_design.single_target_eprocess: For Bernoulli mismatch M_t, likelihood-ratio factors against p0=.005 using p1=.10: mismatch factor=20; match factor=.9/.995. Threshold=100 gives a Ville alarm level <=.01 under the stated iid or per-step conditional p<=.005 null.
degradation_monitor_design.mixture_eprocess: Predeclare equal mixture of p1 in {.02,.05,.10,.20}; each component is a valid e-process under the same p<=.005 conditional null, so the fixed mixture is valid and covers a wider range of degradation speeds.
degradation_monitor_design.state_transition: Fingerprint begins in certified/hedging-eligible only from the separate admission rule. If its degradation e-process crosses the alarm threshold or a deterministic fingerprint/output mismatch is directly observed, immediately demote that fingerprint to canonical-attempt/unresolved mode. Do not wait for aggregate parent evidence to recover. Recertification uses new/disjoint admission evidence or deterministic-contract restoration.

worker_local_degradation_stress.status: Synthetic Bernoulli Monte Carlo; not a measured mismatch rate for any serving system.
interpretation: The targeted p1=.10 detector is fast for severe degradation but weak for p=.02 over 1000 groups.
The fixed mixture gives broad coverage: in this stress it detected p=.02 by 2000 groups in ~99.6% of runs while retaining fast detection for p=.05-.20.
The null alarm rate is below the 1% Ville bound in these simulations. Monte Carlo is only a sanity check; validity comes from the e-process construction under the stated conditional null.

rare_stratum_burst_policy.problem: A rare high-risk fingerprint can be hidden indefinitely by a global pooled mismatch monitor because abundant low-risk traffic dilutes its evidence. The same rare stratum can later dominate an evaluation workload.
policy: Maintain a separate admission/degradation state per deterministic fingerprint or predeclared validity stratum; no traffic-weighted pooling for a smaller epsilon bound.
A parent-level monitor may trigger a broad system alarm, but cannot keep a child hedging-eligible when the child is unknown, drifted, or individually alarmed.
If per-child traffic is too sparse to establish a statistical bound, use deterministic contract coverage as the parent fallback; otherwise fail closed for that child.

Allocate conformance probes deliberately toward low-volume/high-impact strata instead of sampling only in proportion to production traffic; this is an engineering allocation policy and any resulting statistical selection must be accounted for by the monitor design.
rare_stratum_burst_policy.expected_tradeoff: Stratification increases certification sample cost but prevents aggregate-good/child-bad masking. The correct comparison is certification cost versus the statistical validity loss of pooling, not pooled interval width alone.

new_measurement_validity_rules: A pooled empirical mismatch rate is descriptive observability, not a conditional identity certificate for every child stratum.

Conservative parent fallback must be conservative by construction: a domain-wide deterministic guarantee, a structural worst-case child bound, or a simultaneous conditional model. Unknown children otherwise fail closed.

Keep admission and degradation logically separate: admission asks whether fastest hedging may start; degradation monitoring asks whether an admitted fingerprint should be demoted. A non-alarm is not fresh proof of determinism.
Use fixed/predeclared mixture e-processes when degradation magnitude is unknown; do not choose the p1 component after seeing mismatch history without accounting for that selection.
Rare strata require their own state or deliberate probes. Global traffic-weighted monitoring can be operationally reassuring while statistically invalid for a workload concentrated in a rare stratum.
scope_guards: The degradation simulations assume Bernoulli mismatch probabilities with no distribution shift inside each condition. The e-process remains valid only under the stated iid/conditional null; real serving dependence must be represented in the null or handled by deterministic contract/fail-closed logic.
Alarm-time medians are conditional on alarm and are not expected detection delays over all runs.
The mixture result is tied to p0=.005, the four fixed p1 values, threshold100 and the tested horizons. Different engineering targets require redesign.
A hierarchical statistical model may support valid borrowing if it supplies the required simultaneous/conditional guarantees; this checkpoint rejects naive pooling, not all hierarchical inference.

frontier.action: Build a joint admission/demotion state machine with explicit global risk accounting across many fingerprints: allocate calibration/alarm budgets, prevent repeated recertification from resetting lifetime error, and compare deterministic-contract coverage with statistical epsilon certification.

Optimize deliberate conformance allocation across rare/common strata under a fixed probe budget, minimizing the number of uncertified evaluation attempts while preserving per-stratum conditional guarantees.

Stress the mixture degradation monitor under bursty/non-iid mismatch and fingerprint changes. Derive a null in terms of predictable conditional mismatch bounds so correlated bursts are covered rather than assumed away.

Combine the stratum-specific epsilon bound with finite-horizon paired-sign betting under epsilon uncertainty and demotion mid-audit; require fail-closed unresolved behavior when a fingerprint alarms during an evaluation.

frontier.exact_next_action: Construct a lifetime-valid multi-fingerprint admission/demotion state machine: calibration and degradation e-processes must not reset error budget after recertification, and a mid-audit mismatch alarm must deterministically quarantine remaining fastest-selected outcomes. Compare statistical certification cost against deterministic-contract coverage for rare strata.
